cards.text: Hosea is a prophet, and the word of the LORD came to him (Hos 1:1). This message is for the people of Israel, and it opens by shutting a celebration down: 'Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation like the nations…'

cards.question: Hosea tells Israel not to celebrate like the nations do. Why not?

answers.text: They've been unfaithful to their God
They just lost their king in battle
Their harvest came in far too late

cards.text: Hosea calls it playing the harlot against God, making 'love for hire on every threshing floor.' Keep your eye on those threshing floors, friend, because Hosea's not done with them.

cards.question: True or false: The threshing floor and the winepress will keep feeding Israel.

cards.text: Then it gets heavier: 'They will not remain in the land of the LORD…' Ephraim, Hosea's other name for Israel, will return to Egypt.

cards.question: Ephraim is headed back to Egypt. Where else will they end up eating unclean food?

cards.text: Out there, no more wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices won't please Him. Hosea says they'll be 'like the bread of mourners; all who eat will be defiled.'

cards.question: Hosea says Israel's bread will be for themselves. Where won't it go?

answers.text: Into the house of the LORD
Out to the poor at the gate

cards.text: Then Hosea asks, 'What will you do on the appointed day, on the day of the LORD’s feast?' That's the timer going off on the BIG day, and you never even mixed the dough.

cards.question: Hosea says even if Israel flees destruction, Egypt will gather them. Which city will bury them?
True or false: Hosea pictures Israel's tents overrun with thorns.

cards.text: Now the alarm sounds: 'The days of punishment have come; the days of retribution have arrived—let Israel know it.'

cards.question: God's prophet is warning Israel. What does the prophet get called?

cards.text: And Hosea says why: because Israel's iniquity and hostility are so great. That's like yelling 'The OVEN'S SMOKING!' and the whole kitchen turns around and says, 'Who let this guy in?'
Hosea calls the prophet Ephraim's watchman, along with Hosea's God. Then he adds, 'Hostility is in the house of his God!'

cards.question: Ephraim's watchman is on the job. What lies on all his paths?

answers.text: A trap set to catch him

cards.text: Hosea says they have 'deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah…' That's the town where a terrible crime happened back in Judges 19.

cards.question: He will remember their ___; He will punish their sins.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks: 'I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness.' That's like finding a warm cookie in the back of a junk drawer, and believe me, friend, I'd REMEMBER that.
He saw their fathers as the first figs of the season. But they went to Baal-peor, where Israel joined in worshiping Baal back in Numbers 25, and 'consecrated themselves to Shame…'

cards.question: Israel's fathers gave themselves to Shame at Baal-peor. What did they become?

answers.text: As detestable as what they loved
As strong as the nations around them
As free as birds in the wilderness

cards.text: Then the LORD says, 'Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird…'

cards.question: Ephraim's glory flies away like a bird. What will Ephraim have none of?

cards.text: Even if they raise children, the LORD says He will bereave them of each one.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says woe to Ephraim when He turns away from them.

cards.text: The LORD says He has seen Ephraim like Tyre, planted in a meadow. Tyre was a rich trading city on the sea (Ezek 27:33).

cards.question: True or false: Ephraim, pictured like Tyre planted in a meadow, just keeps on thriving.

cards.text: Then the prophet speaks to the LORD: 'Give them, O LORD—what will You give?'

cards.question: The prophet asks what the LORD will give Ephraim. What does he land on?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks again: 'All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them.' Hosea has already warned Israel about Gilgal (Hos 4:15).

cards.question: Because of their wicked deeds, where will the LORD drive Ephraim from?
True or false: The LORD says all of Ephraim's leaders are rebellious.

cards.text: Next, the picture turns into a plant in the ground: 'Ephraim is struck down…'

cards.question: Ephraim is struck down; their ___ is withered; they cannot bear ___.

cards.text: Then the prophet sums it up: 'My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him…'

cards.question: Rejected by God, what will Israel become among the nations?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 has a dash outside a quotation: "Now the alarm sounds: 'The days of punishment have come; the days of retribution have arrived—let Israel know it.'"

rule.text: No em dashes or en dashes to make a sentence longer.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 has a dash outside a quotation: "Then the prophet speaks to the LORD: 'Give them, O LORD—what will You give?'"

rule.text: No em dashes or en dashes to make a sentence longer.

findings.problem: Card 5 says Ephraim is 'Hosea's other name for Israel' with no reference. This is a fact from outside the passage. Other cards give a reference for outside facts, such as Judges 19 for Gibeah and Ezek 27:33 for Tyre.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The core action of Hos 9:7 is a messenger being called a fool and insane for his warning. The punchline 'Who let this guy in?' treats the warner as an outsider who doesn't belong, not as someone who has lost his mind. The joke doesn't share the action of the text. A line like 'Somebody check on Dorin, he's lost it' would match.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Hos 9:13b says 'Ephraim will bring out his children for slaughter.' No card tells this line. The true/false card only tests the vague statement that Ephraim 'just keeps on thriving,' and the next card jumps to v14. The baker never learns what actually happens in the second half of v13.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 12 says 'Hosea has already warned Israel about Gilgal (Hos 4:15).' In Hos 4:15, 'Do not go to Gilgal' comes right after 'may Judah not become guilty,' so the text leaves open who is being warned. Saying the warning was to Israel states more than the text does.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: Hos 9:15 says 'I will no longer love them.' This is one of the heaviest lines in the passage, and no card tells it. Cards 13 and 14 cover the drive from My house and the rebellious leaders, then the walkthrough moves on to v16.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The right answers 'root' and 'fruit' are plant parts. The card before them has just said 'the picture turns into a plant in the ground.' The wrong answers 'rain,' 'gold' and 'swords' are not the same kind of thing, and in a plant picture 'gold' and 'swords' are obviously out. Use wrong answers that fit the plant picture without being near-matches.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Many story cards are a bare lead-in and a quote, with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Examples are stop 1 cards 5, 7, 12 and 15, and stop 2 cards 4, 6, 10, 15 and 17. Stop 2 has only one moment of personality, in card 1. A passage of judgment calls for a different kind of voice, not no voice at all.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
